newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end firmer, Olivetti off day highs.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end firmer, Olivetti off day highs.

text.p: Italian shares ended firmer but off day's highs on Thursday in a session marked by a two-hour disruption due to a technical fault and the suspension of Olivetti for most of the day, dealers said.
The all-share Mibtel index closed 0.75 percent up at 9,587 and the Mibtel blue chip index closed 0.94 percent higher at 14,368.

Shares in troubled high-tech group Olivetti, suspended limit up in pre-bourse price-matching, resumed trading only when trading limits were widened to 20 percent. After starting 17.6 percent up at 600 lire, the stock ended the day 11.76 percent higher at 570 lire in volume of over 71 million shares.

Operators had mixed views over the naming of a new chief executive on Wednesday night after Francesco Caio resigned after less than three months at the helm, but the market was fairly sceptical about the possibility of a speedy solution to the loss-making group's problems.
"There are still a lot of questions to be answered, starting with that about possible alliances," one operator said.

Some stocks moved on the imminent expiry of Fib30 futures and options. Mobile phone operator TIM rose 3.28 percent to 2,991 lire, mainly due to shortcovering, one dealer said. "But there could have been a deal linked to arbitrage," another said.
Fiat ended 0.05 percent lower at 4,189 lire. The carmaker had seen selling pressure in recent sessions ahead of half-yearly results which had been expected to show a fall.
After the bourse closed Fiat announced first half 1996 pre-tax profit of 1.547 trillion lire against a previous 2.153 trillion.
State energy giant Eni gained 1.13 percent to 7,000 lire ahead of a second tranche public share offering next month.
Media group Mediaset gained 1.09 percent to 7,314 lire and insurer Mediolanum was 1.25 percent up at 16,748. Both recently quoted firms are part of Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest empire.
